name: MD-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Glenn Ivey running with a large cash advantage
Prediction markets price near-certain Democratic win
No polls or expert ratings, but fundamentals dominate
model.rationale: A D+39 district with an incumbent Democrat who has raised over $670,000 against an underfunded Republican leaves little room for doubt, and markets price the race at 97% Democratic. The forecast stays at a roughly 32-point Democratic margin.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or redistricting change could tighten the race, but nothing in the current evidence suggests it.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maryland's 4th District is one of the most Democratic-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of D+39. Incumbent Glenn Ivey is running for reelection after winning the nomination, holding about $459,000 in cash on hand from $674,000 raised. His Republican opponent, George McDermott, shows no reported fundraising, and a Green Party candidate is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, but prediction markets put Democratic chances at roughly 97%. The combination of the district's overwhelming lean, incumbency, and financial advantage makes this a Safe Democratic seat, with the only real question being the size of the margin.
